# Ptah public information

## Identity and concept

Ptah (pronounced ピタ, Pita) is an architecture development environment and semantic CAD project, initially focused on Japanese timber housing.

Guiding statement: “建築をビルドする。そのビルド結果を、人間が確かめられる。” (Build architecture. Humans can inspect and verify the build results.)

Ptah aims to support direct human design and eventual AI-agent operations through the same architecture model and execution of defined rules. Architecture is represented as meaningful building elements, specifications, relationships, constraints, decisions, and rationale, not merely geometric lines and surfaces.

The term Build refers to deriving a building model and artifacts from design descriptions and rules. It does not mean autonomous physical construction. Derivation, validation, and human authorization are separate.

## Development direction

These are development goals, not general-release feature claims:

1. Model spaces, structural members, openings, storeys, constraints, and specifications as meaningful entities.
2. Apply design and construction Methods / Rules to derive model elements.
3. Preserve unknown, ambiguous, conflicting, and undecided states.
4. Track consumed inputs, derived results, decisions, dependencies, and rationale.
5. Derive 2D and 3D presentations, drawings, and eventually quantity and estimate outputs.
6. Support verification, comparison, and human review of what changed and why.
7. Eventually offer interfaces for AI agents, external tools, and WASM plugins.

The project uses Rust and prioritizes real timber-building cases over generic infrastructure.

## Current public status

Status date: 2026-11-23.

- Ptah is in development. Internal implementations and verification exist for building models, rules, and 2D/3D drawing representations.
- There is no general-public binary download.
- No public API, MCP server, plugin system, or AI-agent control interface is offered.
- WASM plugin support and source-release/licensing terms are not yet publicly available or finalized.
- Capabilities, formats, supported environments, and availability may change.
- No claim of comprehensive professional fitness, structural safety, legal compliance, or construction readiness is made.

## Scope boundaries

This public site does not publish Ptah application source code, private drawings or building files, personal information, internal validation fixtures, or unreleased download links.

## Brand

The official mark evokes the twin peaks of Mount Tsukuba, with the right peak slightly higher, and the word “ptah”. Dawn-gradient and monochrome versions are used according to context.
